purpose: Test a reusable cross-package Quest handoff where a foreground XR app opens a separate 2D questionnaire panel, the panel receives input, and the same XR app returns to foreground after the panel closes.
authority_boundary: The questionnaire app is a normal Quest 2D panel app, not HOME, device owner, shell, or XR compositor authority.
The foreground XR app owns the product launch request.
Termux and ADB are lab fallback tools only and are not required for the product path.
The test must not use force-stop, package killing, hidden launchers, or Meta menu navigation as the normal return path.

preflight.label: Activate Quest workflow
preflight.command: Operator step: activate the team's Meta Quest workflow for live headset operations before installs, launches, screenshots, logcat, or ADB.

preflight.label: Install XR caller
preflight.command: Operator step: install a test XR app that logs OpenXR state and has a visible Open Questionnaire command.

preflight.label: Install questionnaire panel
preflight.command: Operator step: install a separate questionnaire APK with an exported Quest 2D panel activity.

preflight.label: Record baseline
preflight.command: Record headset model, OS version, current foreground surface, recovery route, and whether ADB or a shell lease is active.

start.label: Launch XR app
start.command: Operator step: launch the XR caller app through the normal Quest app route.

start.label: Open questionnaire
start.command: Inside the XR app, invoke the app-owned command that starts the questionnaire panel with a session id and return PendingIntent.

start.label: Answer questionnaire
start.command: Interact with the focused 2D panel using normal Quest input and submit or cancel the questionnaire.

start.label: Return to XR
start.command: Use the questionnaire panel's Back to XR control; it should invoke the supplied return route and finish only the panel activity.

status.label: Panel focus
status.command: Confirm the questionnaire panel is foregrounded and receives Quest input while the XR app remains alive.

status.label: XR session state
status.command: Record the XR app's OpenXR session state before launch, while the panel is focused, and after return.

status.label: Foreground readback
status.command: Record foreground package/activity before launch, during questionnaire focus, and after return using the active Quest workflow provider.

status.label: No product-path ADB
status.command: Confirm the product-path pass did not use adb shell am start, force-stop, package kill, or Meta menu navigation for the handoff.

stop.label: Close questionnaire
stop.command: If still open, close the questionnaire through its own UI or Android Back.

stop.label: Return to known surface
stop.command: Return to a known operator-approved surface using the normal recovery route for the session.

cleanup.label: Stop lab-only helpers
cleanup.command: Stop any optional logcat, capture, Termux, or ADB helper started specifically for the run.

cleanup.label: Verify no force-stop dependency
cleanup.command: Record whether cleanup used force-stop; if yes, classify it as cleanup only, not part of the handoff result.

cleanup.label: Sanitize evidence
cleanup.command: Keep raw logs, screenshots, device serials, private package IDs, local paths, pairing data, and generated APKs out of public artifacts.

evidence: Sanitized run summary with headset model family and OS version.
Foreground surface before launch, during questionnaire focus, and after return.
OpenXR session state transition summary for the XR app.
Process liveness summary for XR and questionnaire packages.
Classification of any protected prompt, controller requirement, or launch failure.
Statement that product-path return used the questionnaire return route rather than ADB, force-stop, package kill, or Meta menu navigation.

risks.risk: The XR app may lose OpenXR FOCUSED state while the 2D panel owns input.
risks.recovery: Treat VISIBLE or paused-but-alive state as expected during panel focus; fail only if the XR app tears down or cannot regain focus after panel close.

risks.risk: The questionnaire return route may create a duplicate XR activity instead of resuming the existing one.
risks.recovery: Use a caller-provided PendingIntent, stable launch mode, and reorder/single-top flags; record task behavior in the run summary.

risks.risk: A package-name fallback can return to the wrong app or fail under package visibility limits.
risks.recovery: Prefer a caller-provided return PendingIntent; use configured package/activity fallback only as an explicit secondary route.

risks.risk: ADB launch can make the lab pass look stronger than the product path really is.
risks.recovery: Classify any adb shell am start or input-keyevent usage as lab fallback evidence, not the product-path handoff.

notes: See docs/xr-questionnaire-panel-handoff.md for the public-safe contract and manifest sketch.
This recipe is a test checklist, not proof that the cross-package handoff has passed on a real headset.
